topics.label: Course introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context within the cancer lecture series, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetic, environmental, and stochastic factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core concepts of cancer causation by examining the interplay between genetic predisposition, environmental exposures, and stochastic mutations across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how microbial pathogens and viral infections contribute to oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical agents and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce direct or indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and host susceptibility in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors like tumour promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental stages facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches to identifying carcinogens and evaluating their risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reiterating its key themes on cancer causation and risk assessment.
